column2: Branch (fill one copy of this sheet per branch):
PRIMARY KPIs  -  the scoreboard success is judged on

column5: Measured maximum deliverable visits per week versus what is actually delivered. The initiative's core deliverable: capacity becomes a defensible number. Higher utilization is better, up to a safe ceiling.
Share of clinically appropriate referrals declined for lack of capacity, and the admissions / average daily census recovered when it falls. Lower turn-down is better.
Share of clinical labor delivered at a premium (agency, PRN, overtime) because capacity was not visible where it sat idle. Lower is better.
Share of PDGM 30-day periods that fall below the visit threshold and forfeit the full-period payment. Lower is better.
Annualized clinical-staff attrition and the cost to replace. Predictable schedules, balanced loads, and continuity reduce it. Lower is better.

column2: SECONDARY KPIs  -  the leading indicators that move first and explain the primaries

column5: Elapsed time from referral to first billable visit, measured against the 48-hour standard. Leading indicator of referral capture. Lower is better.
Scheduled visits not completed as planned, for any reason. Feeds LUPA exposure and rework. Lower is better.
Share of a patient's visits delivered by their primary clinician. Feeds CAHPS / value-based purchasing and retention. Higher is better.
How much of the set schedule changes before it is worked. An early warning for instability that predicts turnover and misses. Lower is better.
Evenness of true load across clinicians once acuity and travel are counted. Imbalance is an early turnover signal. More balance is better.
Delivered work versus realistic potential, and the share of the day spent in care versus driving. Explains movement in utilization and cost per visit. Higher is better.
Time work waits at hand-offs across the intake-to-care pipeline. Feeds SOC timeliness and missed visits. Lower is better.
How much scheduling actually runs through the product. MVP-critical: if it is not used, none of the other metrics move. Higher is better.
